result.summary: Updates `-acceptnonstdtxn=1` on test networks so that mempool policy checks only enforce potential consensus script flags rather than standard non-mandatory script verify flags. It replaces a heuristic flag-mask test in `CheckInputScripts` with an explicit enum designating whether a check is for a block or a mempool acceptance, and introduces compile-time validation to verify that consensus script flags are always covered by standard script verify flags.
result.problem: On test networks, configuring `-acceptnonstdtxn=1` allowed non-standard transaction structures into the mempool, but policy script verification still unconditionally enforced `STANDARD_SCRIPT_VERIFY_FLAGS`. Developers testing future soft forks or experimental transactions using opcodes like `OP_SUCCESS` or `OP_NOPx` were unable to relay or test transactions in mempools without mining them directly into blocks.
evidence: Author PR description: 'This PR changes -acceptnonstdtxn=1 so that it also skips the non-mandatory script checks, allowing txs that (eg) use OP_NOPx or OP_SUCCESS into the mempool. This remains only available on test nets.'
Commit 54b11fe9c9 updates MemPoolAccept to use chainstate consensus script flags instead of STANDARD_SCRIPT_VERIFY_FLAGS when require_standard is disabled.
result.scope_notes: Touches validation logic in src/validation.cpp by adding the CheckInputScriptsFor enum to distinguish mempool from block validation error reporting and introducing a consteval ConsensusScriptVerifyFlags helper.
result.card: Allows transactions violating standard non-mandatory script verification flags (such as OP_NOPx or OP_SUCCESS) to be admitted into the mempool and relayed when running with -acceptnonstdtxn=1 on test networks. Previously, test network nodes with non-standard transaction acceptance enabled still enforced STANDARD_SCRIPT_VERIFY_FLAGS during policy checks. The PR also replaces a script flag-mask heuristic in CheckInputScripts with an explicit block-versus-mempool enum and adds compile-time assertions ensuring standard flags subsume all consensus flags.

risk.why: A mistake in defining consensus flags or handling CheckInputScripts error reporting could lead to accepting block-invalid transactions into the mempool or misreporting block validation failures.
